status_note: The ten targeted JumpTable::sanityCheck/recoverAddresses projections are byte-identical MATCH against locked Ghidra 12.0.4. The recover-driven reject case observes exact LowlevelError text and all address/load/loadcount mutations before the failed sanity check, plus the absence of collapse; the successful truncation case observes the warning and recover>build>sanity>collapse sequence; the equal-address case proves LoadTable ordering compares addr only. Fixture overall remains MISMATCH under JUMPTABLE-PIPELINE-0001 because production Rugra flow/funcdata still consumes the legacy bool/Option adapter instead of the typed result.

decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: sanityCheck receives vector<int4>* loadcounts and passes the same object by reference to JumpModel::sanityCheck; addresstable, loadpoints and partialTable are JumpTable members mutated in place and remain observable when JumptableThunkError/LowlevelError unwinds. Rugra passes Option<&mut Vec<i32>> and the member Vecs directly, returns JumpTableRecoveryError::{Thunk,Lowlevel} with the exact explain text, and deliberately does not roll back model mutations on Err.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: sanityCheck order is override return -> snapshot size -> isReachable -> single-entry thunk check -> model sanity -> successful-size warning. isReachable examines at most two predecessor levels (i=0,1), requiring exactly one in-edge and a two-way constant CBRANCH guard. recoverAddresses performs recoverModel/getTableSize/buildAddresses/sanityCheck in that order and only then collapses collected loads. The fixture records its collapse marker immediately after recoverAddresses returns successfully, when the emitted post-state proves the internal collapse completed; reject emits recover>build>sanity, no marker, and uncollapsed post-state.
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: The saved table size is captured after the override early return and before reachability/thunk/model checks, and is consulted only after model sanity succeeds. The absolute target/op offset difference is computed once for a single entry and compared strictly greater than 0xffff. Per-case recover/build/sanity counters start at zero. Recover-path loadcounts start empty and are captured after build and again after sanity: success_truncate/model_reject expose 2,2,7, sort_equal_addr exposes 3,3, and override exposes 2.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: The thunk discriminator is keyed first by addresstable.size()==1, then target offset==0 or unsigned absolute offset difference from indirect->getAddr() > 0xffff; multi-entry tables bypass it. Locked LoadTable::operator< at jumptable.hh:59 returns addr < op2.addr and has no size/num tie-break. collapseTable's sole sort consumer uses that strict-weak ordering; equal-address 0x4000/8/2 and 0x4000/4/3 remain comparator-equivalent, while later collapse decisions still inspect size and adjacency.

overlays.policy: primary file under test; raw SHA-256 pinned by comparand.jumptable_overlay_sha256

single_target_boundary.covers: zero throws typed thunk with exact 'Likely thunk'; near succeeds; a difference exactly 0xffff succeeds; 0x10000 throws typed thunk; model sanity is skipped on both thunk cases.

multi_target_bypass.covers: A two-target table containing zero and a target 0x20000 away bypasses the table-level thunk discriminator and reaches model sanity once.

partial_before_thunk.covers: A collapsed constant-false predecessor marks partialTable before the zero single target throws, and the partial mutation remains visible at the thunk catch point.

override_short_circuit_and_collapse.covers: recoverAddresses reuses the override model, builds a zero target, sanityCheck returns before reachability/thunk/model sanity, partial stays false, and internal loadcounts are 2. The successful-return marker yields recover>build>collapse, while the post-state proves the internal collapse produced 0x3000/4/2.

successful_truncation_warning_order.covers: A recover-driven model is transiently retained for model selection, then acts as non-override during sanity: it truncates two addresses to one, appends load 0x3008 and loadcount 7, and returns true. The exact WARNING comment is emitted; the successful-return marker and post-state prove recover>build>sanity>collapse, with internal loadcounts 2,2,7.

lowlevel_partial_mutation.covers: The actual recoverAddresses path transiently retains the fixture model for selection, then calls recover/build/non-override model sanity; sanity truncates two addresses to one, appends load 0x3008 and loadcount 7, and returns false. LowlevelError text is exact, events stop at recover>build>sanity, all mutations survive, warning is absent, and the absent successful-return marker plus post-state prove loadpoints remain uncollapsed.

equal_address_load_sort_key.covers: Successful recover/collapse receives 0x4000/8/2, 0x4000/4/3 and 0x4010/8/1. The first two compare equivalent because LoadTable::operator< uses addr only; size/num do not reorder them, and the emitted post-collapse order matches the locked oracle.

production_typed_stage_consumption.covers: Ghidra Funcdata::stageJumpTable catches JumptableThunkError separately and returns fail_thunk; Rugra production callers still consume recover_addresses/try_recover through bool/Option compatibility adapters, so the typed recovery mode is lost before the production stage.

residuals.detail: The typed classifier and direct recoverAddresses projection match, but this task's write-set excludes flow/funcdata; production must still migrate to try_recover_classified/recover_addresses_classified and preserve FailThunk separately from FailNormal.

branches.detail: Legacy bool/Option compatibility collapses both JumpTableRecoveryError variants, whereas locked stageJumpTable has distinct JumptableThunkError and LowlevelError catch clauses.
